title: Presence Over Position
goal: Identify where our pursuit of position overshadows our pursuit of presence with God and take steps to realign our focus this week.
scripture_instructions: Split the reading of Mark 9:30-50 between two people. Have the first reader cover verses 30-41, and the second reader finish with verses 42-50. Allow each section to sink in after reading.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: Share an experience where you found yourself striving for recognition or position.
icebreakers.note: Helps introduce the theme of pursuing position versus recognizing presence.

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: Think about a time when unexpected circumstances reshaped your outlook on life.
icebreakers.note: Encourages storytelling and reflection on personal growth through adversity.

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: Describe a situation where you felt God's presence during a challenging time.
icebreakers.note: Directly connects personal faith experiences to the sermon's message on presence.

sections.title: Arguing Greatness
sections.setup: The disciples argue about their greatness right after Jesus predicts His suffering. This discussion highlights a common tendency to seek security and worth through position rather than presence. Jesus uses this moment to teach the values of servanthood and humility as pathways to true greatness, countering societal norms of status.

questions.ask: When have you found yourself seeking position over experiencing presence, and what was the impact?
questions.lead: The disciples missed Jesus' presence while clinging to their positions.

questions.ask: Identify a recent instance where you served without seeking recognition. How did it affect you?
questions.lead: Jesus uses a child to illustrate true greatness as serving others.

questions.ask: Think of a time you welcomed someone who could offer you nothing in return. What did you learn from it?
questions.lead: Recognizing and welcoming those with no status is key to Jesus' teaching.

questions.ask: What current pursuit of position might be distracting you from truly trusting Jesus now?
questions.lead: Position often promises security but distracts from trust in Jesus' presence.

reflection_questions: When have I found myself seeking position over experiencing presence, and what was the impact on me?
Identify a recent instance where I served without seeking recognition. How did it affect me?
Think of a time I welcomed someone who could offer me nothing in return. What did I learn from it?
What current pursuit of position might be distracting me from truly trusting Jesus now?

sections.title: Handling Sin and Temptation
sections.setup: In this passage, Jesus addresses the serious nature of sin, urging His followers to deal with it directly, despite the potential difficulty. Through strong metaphors, He emphasizes that personal and communal holiness cannot be taken lightly. The hyperbolic language is meant to wake us up to the urgency of cutting sin out of our lives rather than managing or overlooking it.

questions.ask: Reflect on a sin you’ve been managing instead of addressing directly. What step can you take to 'cut it off'?
questions.lead: Jesus uses harsh images to convey the seriousness of dealing with sin.

questions.ask: Where have you underestimated the impact of a 'manageable' sin in your life, and what has been the cost?
questions.lead: Sin often disguises itself as manageable but is destructive in nature.

questions.ask: How does understanding the consequences of sin challenge you to examine your life differently?
questions.lead: Jesus speaks about the reality of hell to emphasize the consequences of unchecked sin.

questions.ask: What immediate steps can you take today to remove a sin or influence that diverges you from God?
questions.lead: The urgency in Jesus' message is clear: act now to address sin.

Where have I underestimated the impact of a 'manageable' sin in my life, and what has been the cost?
How does understanding the consequences of sin challenge me to examine my life differently?
What immediate steps can I take today to remove a sin or influence that diverges me from God?

sections.title: True Greatness
sections.setup: Jesus challenges cultural norms by redefining greatness as a life of service and humility. He encourages the disciples to live for an audience of one and to find significance through their devotion to God, not through societal recognition. This section calls us to examine our ambitions, highlighting that true success lies in prioritizing God’s kingdom over earthly respect.

questions.ask: In what area of your life can you serve without expectation of return this week?
questions.lead: Jesus calls us to serve with no agenda and to be humble.

questions.ask: How can you begin to shift your mindset from competition to partnership in your ministry or work environment?
questions.lead: Avoid being territorial as John was, recognizing and celebrating God’s work beyond personal teams.

questions.ask: Where is God calling you to be a distinctive preservative, influencing without watering down your faith?
questions.lead: Jesus suggested to stay salty as a preservative in society, retaining distinctive attributes of the kingdom.

questions.ask: When are you most tempted to pursue personal success over God's calling, and what can you do to shift this?
questions.lead: Jesus redefined ambition by focusing on Godly fulfillment over personal praise.

reflection_questions: In what area of my life can I serve without expectation of return this week?
How can I begin to shift my mindset from competition to partnership in my ministry or work environment?
Where is God calling me to be a distinctive preservative, influencing without watering down my faith?
When am I most tempted to pursue personal success over God's calling, and what can I do to shift this?

closing_go_around: Each man names one area where he will prioritize presence over position this week and one step he’ll take to ensure that.
prayer: Have each man pray for the man to his right, focusing on the courage to prioritize Jesus' presence. The leader will close by reading 1 Peter 1:6-7, highlighting how trials refine faith.

Prompt for specific life examples or personal stories.
Pause the discussion, acknowledge the emotion, and ask if the speaker would like to share more.
Re-center on practical outcomes related to personal presence over public position.

key_themes: Presence vs. Position: Value God's presence over earthly status to find true greatness.
Servanthood: Serve others without expecting anything in return.
Sin's Deception: Recognize and address sin as a serious threat to your spiritual life.
Formation through Trials: See trials as God's way to refine your character.
Staying Salty: Maintain your distinctiveness and preserve the kingdom qualities in your environment.
commitment_prompt: Decide on one specific area this week where you will choose presence over position and ask another man to check in with you before next meeting.
leader_notes: The sermon began with an illustration of Theodore Roosevelt, a man of power and position, who was transformed by his experience in the Badlands. This period of hardship and isolation reshaped him into a courageous leader, ready for the responsibilities of the presidency. It frames our passage because it mirrors the kind of formation Jesus calls His followers to, prioritizing presence and character over status.

In Mark 9:30-50, Jesus shares a deep truth about His coming suffering, yet the disciples are caught up in arguments about greatness. The preacher highlighted this contradiction: Jesus is on His way to the cross, shedding position, while the disciples grasp for it. This irony underpins the passage, where Jesus uses the moment to teach lessons on humility, using a child to symbolize true greatness as serving others selflessly.

The thesis worth keeping at the forefront: True greatness comes not from earthly positions but from the presence with God and serving others. The preacher's outline follows Jesus’ teachings: Serve without an agenda, surrender the impulse to be territorial, stop tolerating sin, and stay salty as a preservative in the world. This outline is the spine of our discussion guide.

Given the group's makeup, anticipate that some men will confidently offer polished answers about servanthood and sin management. However, the 'True Greatness' section is designed to push beyond surface-level reflections and call for tangible admissions of where position-seeking diverts them from God's presence.

First, we should be mindful that discussing personal sin can touch on sensitive areas, so approach with care. Second, there are those currently struggling in 'Badlands' who may lack perspective; empathy is needed here. Third, those presenting a 'showroom faith' may need encouragement to be authentic rather than keeping up appearances. Handle these with pastoral sensitivity.
